source.repro: pnpm exec esbuild --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --target=node22 --outfile=/tmp/lanefit.mjs plugins/linear-comparative-view/benches/multiwayLaneFit.probe.ts && node /tmp/lanefit.mjs, from the repo root (it rewrites this file) - the eight hosted hg38 liftOver PIFs of demos/hg38_vertebrates over a 1.2 Mb hg38 window walking chr17:10-25 Mb in 100 kb steps (151 steps, 1500 px), each step's decisions carried into the next, the whole walk fetched at once.
source.notes:
HOW WIDE A LANE DRAWS THROUGH A DUPLICATION-RICH STRETCH. `mean rung` is the lane's average width as a multiple of the anchor window; `wide steps` counts steps drawn at 3x or wider, where a collinear block squeezes to a third of the anchor's width and its ribbons fan. `undrawn` is the share of the anchor bp the lane places on its drawn contig whose placement falls wholly outside the drawn frame, so it draws no ribbon.

BEFORE 2026-10-11, measured with this walk on the then-main code: wide steps 32/41/53/63/73/39/18/46 (365 in all), mean rungs 1.36-6.13, rung changes 124, oscillations 4, undrawn 4.5-27.3%. Two things inflated the width. The fit spanned the min to the max of every placement within `OUTLIER_REACH` of the median, so a 16-23 kb stray chain set the zoom of a lane whose main chains held 95-99% of its bp. And a hole opened between any two lane-adjacent pieces whose anchors sat apart, so two chains meeting at a rearrangement breakpoint opened a hole of the anchor distance between them, 2-7 Mb here, which the opened extent then counted. Holes come off every fetched group, so the rung depended on how far the fetch reached past the viewport: the 17p figure's window (chr17:15,200,014-16,400,014) fetched with a 0.4 Mb pad drew 1/1/5/3/3/3/3/1.5, the published figure exactly, and window-only 1/1/3/1.5/3/3/2/1.5.

WHAT CHANGED. A hole opens only between two pieces of one alignment record (`recordId`, stamped by `clipFeatureToRegion`), or where the lane places the anchor between the two pieces nowhere, which is how the HPRC PIF states the CFHR3-CFHR1 deletion. The rung and centre fit the bulk: the clusters (pieces under a quarter window apart) holding any piece `keepNearMedian` keeps, whole, less `peelEnds`' isolated end clusters up to 5% of the lane's vote evidence; `fitMin`/`fitMax` keep the median-filtered extent. Each of the first two alone over this walk, measured on a prototype that weighed by lane bp: peeling 244 wide steps, 103 changes, 9 oscillations; the record rule 177, 115, 6. The whole-cluster rule moved 8 wide steps (gorGor6, mm39) and fixed the 17p marmoset lane, whose median reach cut its forward block in two on the figure's padded fetch: it drew at 2x with half its bp off the frame. Bounding the alignment shift by the bulk fixed the same lane and was dropped: it held the E. coli operon lanes off their alignment to keep edge genes in view, and the whole-cluster rule alone gives marmoset 3x with both blocks. The 17p window now draws 1/1/1.5/1.5/3/1/1/1 at fetch pads of 0, 0.4 and 1.2 Mb. The oscillations are one-step 1x/1.5x returns at 14.3-14.7 Mb and one 1.5/3/1.5 on rheMac10, where a stray cluster sits on the 5% budget or the cluster gap: the window re-clips the pieces at its edges each step, which moves their weights. Skipping the peel while the held rung still covers the unpeeled bulk was measured and declined: oscillations 9 to 6 and rung changes 87 to 76, but wide steps 67 to 92 and panTro6's mean rung 1.41 to 1.70, and canFam6 kept its three. The grape MCScan walk (multiway-lane-stability) holds its rung changes and oscillations.
